_doc: Category-29 (Edible Fungi) compiler config for tools/standards/compile-cat29.mjs — HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default). Numbers come ONLY from data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, selected per subcategory by explicit scope regex and the strictest applicable credible sovereign maximum, in the row's native (fresh, wet-weight) basis. Occurrence evidence is descriptive market characterisation and can NEVER select an initial limit.
_method_note: native_basis is as_sold (fresh mushroom, wet weight — the basis every sovereign fungi ML is expressed in); reconstitution_8to1 is false so all rows are taken at face value. DRIED mushroom rows (Israel dried mushrooms Pb 1500; Singapore dried mushrooms Cd 1000) are a concentrated, different-basis product and are excluded from both fresh subcategories. Pb and Cd have wild-specific AND cultivated-specific sovereign MLs. tHg, iAs, and tAs bind the general Israel FCS-2016 'fruits and vegetables including mushrooms' MLs (30 / 60 / 1000), which apply to all mushrooms. Total Cr, Cr-VI, Sn, Al, Ni, and MeHg have no fungi ML and resolve to disclosed not-material / control determinations.
_scope_note: THE CULTIVATED / WILD SPLIT IS REAL AND PRESERVED (per the biology: wild fungi hyperaccumulate Cd, Pb, and Hg). Wild mushrooms bind the WILD-SPECIFIC EU 2023/915 and Switzerland VHK 2026 fungi MLs (Pb 800, Cd 500) and NEVER the cultivated numbers (Pb 300, Cd 50) or the generic 'mushrooms except Agaricus/Pleurotus/Lentinula/Lentinus' catch-all (Pb 100, Cd 50). Those generic 'other-mushroom' limits lump wild forest hyperaccumulators with exotic cultivated species and would impose a ceiling far below the wild-specific standard, contradicting the documented accumulation biology; they are excluded from wild. Cultivated mushrooms bind the cultivated fungi MLs (EU/CH/TH/GSO/MERCOSUR-Agaricus Pb 300). THE CULTIVATED CADMIUM ROW IS SPLIT (ratified 2026-08-13, OI-20260813-cultivated-mushroom-cd-split): common cultivated mushrooms (button/Agaricus bisporus) bind Cd 50 (EU 'cultivated fungi, except oyster and shiitake' / CH Agaricus bisporus), while oyster (Pleurotus) and shiitake (Lentinula), which accumulate more cadmium than button mushrooms, bind the looser sovereign Cd 150 (EU 'oyster mushroom and shiitake mushroom' / CH Kulturpilze / Bosnia Lentinula-Pleurotus) in the dedicated cultivated-mushrooms-oyster-shiitake row instead of being ratcheted to 50. Every non-cadmium analyte is identical across the two cultivated rows. MeHg: cultivated fungi grow on controlled substrate and are treated not-material (speciation-bounded by tHg); wild fungi DO have a mercury-methylation pathway and carry a control cell bounded by the total-mercury ceiling, not a not-material dismissal. No government sets a nickel, aluminium, or chromium ML for edible fungi in any jurisdiction.
lineage: Cat-29 government-limit-default compile (HMTc Method v2.0). Anchors: EU Reg. 2023/915 (wild fungi Pb 800 / Cd 500; cultivated fungi Pb 300 / Cd 50; oyster+shiitake Cd 150), Switzerland VHK 2026 (wilde Pilze Pb 800 / Cd 500; Agaricus bisporus Cd 50), MERCOSUR GMC 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 (Agaricus/Pleurotus/Lentinula tAs 300), Israel FCS-2016 (fruits and vegetables including mushrooms: tHg 30 / iAs 60 / tAs 1000). Cultivated-cadmium split (common Cd 50 vs oyster/shiitake Cd 150 → cultivated-mushrooms-oyster-shiitake) ratified 2026-08-13 per OI-20260813-cultivated-mushroom-cd-split.

Ni.control: No credible sovereign government sets a nickel maximum level for edible fungi in any jurisdiction; the EU 2024/1987 nickel regulation enumerates vegetables, legumes, nuts, and cereals but deliberately does not list fungi. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone numeric nickel limit for this matrix; nickel is monitored on the mandatory total-element panel.
Ni.reference_method: Total-element screen by ICP-MS on every lot; investigate any elevated nickel result against grower substrate and provenance.

Cr.control: No credible sovereign government sets a total-chromium contaminant maximum for edible fungi in any jurisdiction (the only register total-Cr MLs are for dairy powder, drinking water, and fertiliser). Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone numeric total-Cr limit for this matrix; total chromium is monitored and hexavalent chromium is controlled by reflex speciation (see Cr-VI).
Cr.reference_method: Total-Cr screen by ICP-MS on every lot; investigate any elevated total-Cr result and reflex-speciate per the Cr-VI control.

Cr-VI.control: No government sets a total-chromium or hexavalent-chromium maximum level for edible fungi in any jurisdiction. Chromium in the fungal matrix is dominated by nutritionally-essential Cr(III), and Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in the organic-rich matrix. Firm control: reflex speciation - any total-Cr result >= 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails; Cr(VI) is never a panel number.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total-Cr screen by ICP-MS; on any result >= 100 ug/kg, Cr(VI) by EN 15192 / EPA 6800 IC-ICP-MS isotope-dilution; LOQ-level quantifiable Cr(VI) = fail.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No regulatory total-Cr or Cr(VI) ML for edible fungi in any jurisdiction; the only register total-Cr MLs are for dairy powder, drinking water, and fertiliser.
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; EU 2024/1987; Switzerland VHK 2026; MERCOSUR GMC 12/2011; Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel FCS-2016; Codex; FDA; China GB 2762

Sn.control: Every government tin maximum level in the register is scoped to canned / tin-coated product; tin migrates from tinplate, and that packaging-migration pathway is the contamination these MLs regulate (India even sets a canned-mushroom Sn ML of 250000 ug/kg). Fresh cultivated and wild mushrooms are not sold in tinplate, so that pathway is absent; any tin present is dietary background rather than tinplate migration. Canned mushrooms route to the canned-foods category and carry the tin ML there.
Sn.reference_method: Mandatory total-element screen by ICP-MS; tin is screened but not a binding numeric ceiling for fresh, non-canned product.
Sn.regulatory_basis: Tin MLs (incl. India canned mushrooms 250000 ug/kg) apply to canned product only; no fresh-fungi Sn ML exists in any jurisdiction.
Sn.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; EU 2024/1987; Switzerland VHK 2026; MERCOSUR GMC 12/2011; Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel FCS-2016; Codex; FDA; China GB 2762

Al.control: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum for edible fungi. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone numeric Al limit for this matrix; naturally present aluminium remains a surveillance issue governed by the additive rules of the markets of sale.
Al.reference_method: Screen total Al by ICP-MS and document any aluminium-containing processing aid; investigate elevated results and comply with all additive rules in markets of sale.

MeHg.control: No government sets a methylmercury ML for edible fungi in any jurisdiction; methylmercury maximum levels exist only for fish and seafood. Cultivated mushrooms grow on controlled substrate and are not a mercury-methylation matrix; any mercury present is bounded by the total-mercury ceiling (Israel FCS-2016 mushrooms tHg 30 ug/kg). No methylmercury ML exists to look up.
MeHg.reference_method: MeHg by GC-ICP-MS / EN 16801 only on a lot whose total mercury approaches the tHg ceiling; cultivated-mushroom methylmercury is characteristically < LOQ.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No regulatory MeHg ML for edible fungi in any jurisdiction; methylmercury MLs are scoped to fish and seafood only. Total mercury is bounded by Israel FCS-2016 mushrooms tHg 30 ug/kg.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; EU 2024/1987; Switzerland VHK 2026; MERCOSUR GMC 12/2011; Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel FCS-2016; Codex; FDA; China GB 2762

cultivated-mushrooms.name: Cultivated mushrooms — common (button/Agaricus bisporus and other common farmed fungi)
cultivated-mushrooms.scope_note: The common-cultivated row binds the strict cultivated-fungi floor: Cd 50 (EU 'cultivated fungi, except oyster and shiitake' / CH Agaricus bisporus), Pb 300, tAs 300, tHg 30, iAs 60. Oyster (Pleurotus) and shiitake (Lentinula) accumulate more cadmium and carry a looser sovereign Cd 150; they are split into the cultivated-mushrooms-oyster-shiitake row (ratified 2026-08-13, OI-20260813-cultivated-mushroom-cd-split) so they certify against the EU Cd 150 carve-out instead of being ratcheted to 50 here. This row's Cd 50 is correct for button/Agaricus; the broad scope resolves to the strictest applicable value, so it is unaffected by the split.

wild-mushrooms.name: Wild mushrooms (foraged fungi — porcini/boletus, chanterelle, morel, wild Agaricus, other wild species)

MeHg.control: Wild fungi DO have a mercury-methylation pathway and are documented mercury hyperaccumulators, so methylmercury is not dismissed as not-material for this subcategory. However, no government sets a methylmercury ML for any fungi in any jurisdiction; the methylmercury fraction is controlled by and bounded by the total-mercury ceiling for wild mushrooms (Israel FCS-2016 mushrooms tHg 30 ug/kg). No methylmercury ML exists to look up, and occurrence cannot supply the number.
MeHg.reference_method: MeHg by GC-ICP-MS / EN 16801 on any wild-mushroom lot whose total mercury approaches the tHg ceiling; wild-fungi methylmercury can be a material fraction of a high total-mercury result and must be characterised on elevated lots.

cultivated-mushrooms-oyster-shiitake.name: Oyster and shiitake mushrooms (cultivated Pleurotus and Lentinula — cadmium accumulators)
cultivated-mushrooms-oyster-shiitake.scope_note: Oyster (Pleurotus) and shiitake (Lentinula edodes) are cultivated fungi that accumulate more cadmium than button mushrooms; EU Reg. 2023/915 ('oyster mushroom and shiitake mushroom' Cd 150), Switzerland VHK 2026 (Kulturpilze Cd 150), and Bosnia (Lentinula/Pleurotus Cd 150) all set a looser cadmium ML for them than the common-cultivated Cd 50 ('cultivated fungi, except oyster and shiitake' / Agaricus bisporus). This row preserves that sovereign carve-out: Cd binds 150, with the Cd analyte_scope dropping the 'except oyster and shiitake' / 'osim ...' / Agaricus-bisporus 50 rows; every other analyte binds the same cultivated-fungi ML as the common row (Pb 300 EU cultivated; tAs 300 MERCOSUR genera; tHg 30 / iAs 60 Israel). No jurisdiction sets oyster/shiitake Cd below 150 (HK Cap 132V shiitake 500 and MERCOSUR/GSO 200 are looser); the retained Cd 50 stricter-unselected flags document the deliberate carve-out. Split ratified 2026-08-13 (OI-20260813-cultivated-mushroom-cd-split).
